title: Elastic Serverless project API key placeholders, references, masks and a bare scheme
summary: The documented ${API_KEY} environment reference, an angle placeholder, a template reference, a masked display and a bare scheme in the Authorization ApiKey slot, and prose that names the slot.
rationale: Elastic's own example sends the key as an environment reference, -H "Authorization: ApiKey ${API_KEY}" (claim encoded-carrier). A reference, a placeholder, a masked display and a bare scheme stand in for a value kept elsewhere and carry none. The case asserts nothing about the id member of the creation response, whose confidentiality is an open question inherited from the stack key. Contract claims cited: serverless-project-api-key/encoded-carrier.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#243). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: these inputs hold no key value. That a reference, placeholder, masked display or bare scheme is not a value is the project's decision; Elastic documents the environment-reference form of the header (carrier fact only).

sources.supports: Once created, you can copy the encoded API key and use it to send requests to the Elasticsearch HTTP API: -H "Authorization: ApiKey ${API_KEY}"

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
